method: fit 2023 -> predict 2024; real bills (HB/SB) only; score = % reduction in mean absolute error vs predicting the session base rate. Positive = better than guessing. Negative = WORSE than guessing.

thresholds.DISQUALIFIED: invalid measurement; see superseded_by for the corrected test and its result
thresholds.CONDITIONAL: helps one outcome, harms the other

dls_tag.note: ADHD round. ADHD/lobbyist frame's strongest tell — the DLS drafting clause after the final semicolon ('; penalty', '; report'). 13 buckets, real variation, no signal.

same_day_batch.note: ADHD round. How many bills the patron filed the same day.

names_locality.note: ADHD round. Catchline names a County/City/Town (a 'courtesy bill'). Only 34 of 2,284, so thin either way.

patron_absence.note: ADHD round. Share of X/A (not voting / abstain) responses. Proposed INDEPENDENTLY by three frames; dead.

filing_recency_band.note: ADHD round. When in the filing window the bill was introduced, as a percentile of HB/SB only. Raw rates 81/82/73/77% — real variation, non-monotonic, no usable signal.

catchline_segments.note: ADHD round. Semicolon count in the catchline. NO VARIATION: 2,274 of 2,284 have exactly 2 segments, so the 'omnibus catchline' tell does not exist in VA data.

how_to_read: Scores are per OUTCOME and do not transfer between them. 'survived' = got out of committee. 'passed' = passed its chamber of origin. Before proposing any stat, grep this file: if it is here, it has been tested and the result stands unless the METHOD changes (new sessions, a fixed definition, or a corrected leak).

blocked_not_tested.section_citations: Needs the count of Code of Virginia sections a bill touches. The CATCHLINE contains no § symbols (0 of 2,284) and full bill text is not published in bulk. NOT TESTED — do not record as dead.
blocked_not_tested.draft_lead_time: Needs the gap between drafting and filing. Full_text_date1 IS the introduction date by construction in every row, so this dataset contains no drafting timeline at all. NOT TESTED.
blocked_not_tested.prior_session_recurrence: Needs a prior session for the TRAINING year too. With only 2023+2024 usable (2022 is partial), the training year has no prior and the feature is constant in training. Needs a THIRD complete session. NOT TESTED.
blocked_not_tested.fiscal_note_footprint: Needs History_description parsing for impact-statement rows; deferred, and would need a structural source before shipping.
blocked_not_tested.cross_chamber_companion: Needs text similarity across chambers; the similarity tooling exists (W2/W3/W4) but catchline-only matching is weak. Deferred.

companion_divergent_majority_standing.design: Companion pairs = same session, both chambers, identical title. DIVERGENT = one side passed, the other did not. Content is held constant, so the surviving side's advantage is attributable to what differs (chamber, committee, patron).
companion_divergent_majority_standing.pool: 11 regular sessions 2017-2027, Open States bulk CSV
caveats: 136 sides had no resolvable party or chamber majority
some title groups hold 3+ bills, so side-counts exceed 2x the pair count
chamber majority derived from the distinct sponsoring roster, not an external roster
companion_divergent_majority_standing.why_it_matters: Every prior test of majority standing had bill CONTENT as a confound. Here the text is identical, so this is the cleanest confirmation available.

Q3_what_gets_a_minority_bill_through.pool: 8,154 minority-patron HB/SB, 11 regular sessions 2017-2027, Open States
Q3_what_gets_a_minority_bill_through.why_it_matters: The only finding so far that names an ACTION rather than describing a situation. Recruiting a majority co-patron, or getting a majority member to carry the companion, is something an advocacy org can actually do.
Q3_what_gets_a_minority_bill_through.caveat: CORRELATIONAL. Bills that attract majority co-patrons may be less partisan to begin with, so the co-patron could be a symptom of an easy bill rather than a cause of the win. TESTABLE against the 504 divergent companion pairs, where text is held constant.
Q3_what_gets_a_minority_bill_through.status: confound test PASSED — cleared for use, with n=42 stated alongside it

confound_test.design: Divergent companion pairs (one side passed, one died) where BOTH chief patrons are in the minority and the two sides DIFFER in whether they have a majority-party co-patron. Text identical, chief-patron standing identical — co-patron composition is the only thing left.
confound_test.verdict: SURVIVES. The 61%-vs-31% headline is not merely a symptom of easy bills attracting co-patrons — with the bill held literally identical, the version carrying a majority co-patron won 3 times in 4.
confound_test.caveat: n=42, small by construction: requiring divergence AND both-minority chiefs AND differing co-patron status is restrictive. The split is lopsided enough that chance is an unlikely explanation, but re-check as sessions accumulate rather than treating it as settled.

findings_2026_08_02._pool: 22,659 HB/SB across 18 Open States sessions (2023S1 excluded as a duplicate of 2023). Companion pairing = exact title OR same subject-half + >=0.6 title-token overlap; recall measured at 92-95% vs abstract-derived truth. 4,424 pairs, 925 divergent.

co_patron_dose_response.read: The FIRST majority co-patron does most of the work: +26 points. After that, diminishing returns.

co_patron_by_chamber.read: Bigger lever in the House (+32) than the Senate (+26) — consistent with the House being the real filter.

seniority.read: Mid-career outperforms veterans in BOTH roles. Unexplained; possibly veterans in the minority carry harder bills.

money_committee_MYTH.read: NO EFFECT with content held constant. Money committees are where expensive bills go, not where bills die.

negative_space_minority_bills.read: Eightfold spread. Every worst is House, every best is Senate.

reintroduction.read: One in three failed bills returns; one in three of those wins. But a returning bill passes BELOW the overall baseline — coming back is not the same as winning.

governor.read: The amendment power is used TWICE as often as the veto, and works more than half the time. The reconvened session matters more than the veto.

where_to_file.read: Same bill, both chambers, one committee passed and its counterpart killed. Directly actionable filing advice.

findings_2026_08_02.topic_source: Virginia titles are 'Topic; what it does.' The subject-half is LIS's own drafting convention, available on all 22,659 bills — 7,825 distinct topics. Not our invention, and it needs no separate subject file (Open States publishes none).

committee_rate_varies_BY_TOPIC.H Finance: overall 37% — real property tax 63%, state income tax 19% (38 of 198). 44-pt spread.
committee_rate_varies_BY_TOPIC.S Education and Health: overall 52% — school boards 62%, certificate of public need 20%. 42-pt spread.
committee_rate_varies_BY_TOPIC.read: A committee's headline rate is often misleading. Validation signal: certificate-of-public-need surfacing as the worst topic in its committee is a well-known VA fight the method found unprompted.

barely matters.income tax, state: 35/147 (24%) vs 10/125 (8%) — 16 pts, but BOTH sides are low

minority_penalty_VARIES_BY_TOPIC.read: THE STRONGEST WAR-ROOM FINDING SO FAR. The minority penalty is not a constant — it runs from 38 points (firearms: 2 of 85 in 18 sessions) to 8 points (ABC). Tells an advocate when patron party is the whole game and when it is nearly irrelevant.
minority_penalty_VARIES_BY_TOPIC.caveat: Topic pooled across committees and chambers; minimum 40 bills per side. Not yet split by control regime.

_answered.house_volume_confound: Rates were used throughout, not counts, so raw volume is normalised (House 4,677 minority bills vs Senate 3,477; 25% vs 39%).
_answered.co_patron_moderate_bill_confound: Ruled out by the identical-text test — 32 of 42 divergent pairs, same bill on both sides.
